en: The Theravāda Vinaya Mahāvibhaṅga,
Chapter on the Training Rules (Sekhiyakaṇḍa)
The Chapter on Standing (Khambhakata-vagga), Chapter 29:
The Training Rule on Receiving Food with Equal Sauce.
At that time, the Buddha, the Blessed One, was dwelling at Sāvatthī in Jeta’s Grove, Anāthapiṇḍika’s monastery.
Now at that time, the group-of-six monks, while receiving almsfood, received a great deal of curry alone... [etc. ...
"The training is to be observed: 'I shall receive almsfood with an equal amount of curry. As for "curry":
it is called curry.
There are two kinds of soups: bean soup and lentil soup, which are taken by the hand.
Almsfood containing equal amounts of rice and soup may be accepted.
Whoever, out of disrespect, accepts a large amount of soup alone, commits an offense of wrong-doing (dukkaṭa).
There is no offense if it was unintentional,
or if there was lack of mindfulness.
For one who does not know,
for one who is ill,
and regarding various flavors.
[It is not an offense] for relatives,
for those who have invited [one to eat],
or for the sake of another.
With one's own wealth,
in times of distress,
for one who is insane,
"For the first offender":
thus ends the ninth training rule.
